classification.difficultyReason: Choose the distinct teams successively from shrinking populations and recognise that the final team is forced, with no division for exchanging teams.

content.prompt: Suppose 18 people are divided into four different teams. The first team has three people, the second team has four people, the third team has five people and the last team has six people. How many ways are there of selecting the teams?

answer.short:
$\binom{18}{3}\binom{15}{4}\binom{11}{5}=514\,594\,080$

Choose the first three teams successively; the remaining six people form the last team.
answer.worked:
Choose each team from the people remaining. After selecting the first three teams, the six remaining people form the last team.

$$\begin{align*}N&=\binom{18}{3}\binom{15}{4}\binom{11}{5}\binom{6}{6}\\N&=816\times1365\times462\times1\\N&=514\,594\,080.\end{align*}$$
